solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Putting together of new gable a mess

indicators.note: new says the letters of the following words are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone describes a collection as a fresh gable thrown together with general mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal working on GABLE A MESS; 'of' just links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a collection, the act or result of gathering things into one place.

clue.text: Tremor caused by dessert wine?

parts.note: afters is British slang for the pudding course
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A jokey suggestion that a sweet wine after dinner could make the ground shake.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British everyday slang for dessert, and HOCK is the British name for Rhine wine. The question mark flags the playful idea of a 'shock' caused by wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A smaller quake following the main earthquake is a kind of tremor.

clue.text: Pronounce "for example"

definitions.meaning: used to introduce an instance, as in 'take, ..., a dog'

explanation.surface: A reading-aloud instruction: speak the words 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to speak words aloud, and the interjection meaning 'let's suppose' or 'for instance'.

clue.text: Most are blown for conductor, perhaps

indicators.note: blown, as in blown apart or scattered by wind, tells us to rearrange the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Most brass instruments are played by blowing, which suits an orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' looks like a description of wind instruments but signals an anagram of MOST ARE; 'perhaps' marks a conductor as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor, is called by this Italian title of mastery.

clue.text: Shine in Ulster broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast originally meant scattered widely, as of seed, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A shiny news item carried on air in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio or TV but signals an anagram of ULSTER, the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the gloss or gleam on a surface, a synonym for shine.

clue.text: Trace female family member holding one

indicators.note: holding says the first word wraps round and contains the second

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A detective's search for a grandmother who is holding someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a tiny amount, as in 'not a grain of truth', just as a trace is.

clue.text: Project worker under notice becoming military aide

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces that follow sit beneath the notice

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public notice
to project is to stick out, or jut
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An office worker on a project, given notice, is moved to an army post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' works because this is a down answer: JUT and ANT are written below AD. 'Project' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is an officer who assists a commanding officer with administration.

clue.text: Herb forming part of healthy meal

indicators.note: forming part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A herb that goes into a nutritious dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a common aromatic culinary herb.

clue.text: Drink readily available after close of business

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first in the answer
close of means the end, so take the final letter of the next word

parts.note: handy means close at hand, ready to use

explanation.surface: A drink is easy to get once the working day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close of business' sounds like the end of the working day, but it only gives the final S of 'business'. SHANDY is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Together, as worker being dealt with

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship
a matter in hand is one currently being handled

explanation.surface: Colleagues team up as one employee's case is processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going hand in hand means jointly or closely together.

clue.text: Drive farm animal

definitions.meaning: to force or push hard, as in driving a nail home

explanation.surface: Herding livestock on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to drive something in by force; and a ram is the uncastrated male sheep.

clue.text: Relevant stuff

definitions.meaning: cloth or fabric, or the substance anything is made from

explanation.surface: Information that bears on the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Material as an adjective means significant to the matter; as a noun it is fabric or substance.

clue.text: Sailor left aunt, worried inside by a spider

indicators.note: inside places the jumbled letters within the sailor-and-a pair

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a seaman

indicators.note: worried, as in shaken or tugged at, tells us to jumble these letters

explanation.surface: A sailor abandons his aunt, who is pestered indoors by a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges L and the aunt's letters into ANTUL; 'inside' sets that within the sailor and the A that 'by' places beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider.

clue.text: Popular pet food

parts.note: hot means in demand, as a hot ticket
a dog is a common pet

explanation.surface: A favourite pet's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pet food; 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage in a soft bread roll is a familiar fast food snack.

clue.text: Stall, bearing right in London thoroughfare

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the stall holds the letter within it

parts.note: a stand is a stall at a market or fair

explanation.surface: A market stall turning right on a busy London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing right' sounds like a direction to turn, but 'bearing' means carrying: STAND carries R. The Strand is a famous street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a major street running from Trafalgar Square towards the City of London.

clue.text: Tout upset priest about ticket, ultimately

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the final letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
ultimately means in the end, picking the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A distressed clergyman complains about ticket touts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PRIEST into TIPSER; 'about' puts it round T, the last letter of 'ticket'. In Britain a tout is someone who sells racing tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tout sells tips on likely winners, the same job as a tipster.

clue.text: Keeper with cosmetics company founder

parts.note: Elizabeth Arden founded the cosmetics firm that bears her name

explanation.surface: A guardian comes with the founder of a cosmetics firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is a guardian or custodian, one who keeps watch over a place or people.

clue.text: Character cutting could be a cheat

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person
sharp means keen-edged, able to cut

explanation.surface: Someone who cuts the deck might be cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests cutting the cards, apt for a card cheat, but it means SHARP; 'Character' is a CARD, a comic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins at card games by trickery.

clue.text: Vixen showing cunning endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: shrewd means astute or wily

explanation.surface: A female fox shows its usual craftiness without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vixen' makes you think of a fox and cunning, but it means a bad-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are old terms for a quarrelsome, bad-tempered woman.

clue.text: Brown belt

definitions.meaning: to brown is to make sun-darkened, as skin in the sun
to belt is to beat or thrash someone

explanation.surface: A martial arts grading: the brown belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a light brown colour or to darken in sun; to tan someone's hide is to thrash them.

clue.text: Dearth, badly managed, causing enmity

indicators.note: something badly managed is in disorder, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A shortage handled poorly causes bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly managed' signals an anagram of DEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred and enmity both name deep hostility or ill will.

clue.text: Greek character on time, he volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek turns up punctually and offers to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet. TA is the Territorial Army, the British army's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bird kept by them, usually

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A bird that a family generally keeps as a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Two golfing terms for pivot

parts.note: a swing is the stroke of the club and a round is a full game of eighteen holes; joined, the pair means turn on the spot

explanation.surface: Two words from golf combine to mean turning about.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a definition by description: name two golf words (the stroke and the full game) and put them together.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on the spot to face the other way is the action of a pivot.
